questions.question: A model sends tool arguments wrapped in a ```json code fence. What should the loop do?
options: Reject it so the model learns the right format
Strip the fence and run the call: the intent is unambiguous
Ask the user what the model meant
questions.explanation: A code fence can't change the meaning of the JSON inside it, so removing it is a lossless repair.

questions.question: The model calls 'look_up' but the tool is named 'lookup'. Why reject with a hint instead of auto-correcting?
options: Guessing tool names can run the wrong tool; a hint lets the model confirm what it meant
The model will never make that mistake twice
questions.explanation: Near-misses can be different tools (delete_file vs delete_files). Repairs must be lossless; a name guess isn't.

questions.question: Why parse Python-style arguments like {'topic': 'K2'} with ast.literal_eval rather than eval?
options: literal_eval only accepts literals and never runs code, so model output can't execute anything
questions.explanation: Tool arguments are untrusted input. literal_eval rejects __import__('os') and any other expression.

questions.question: Which coercion is lossless for a schema field of type number?
questions.explanation: Only a string that is exactly a number converts without guessing. Booleans are not numbers, even though Python treats bool as int.

questions.question: In this lesson's survey, llama3.2 received specific error messages but never retried a tool call. What does that suggest?
options: Whether feedback helps depends on the model; for small models, constrained decoding or fewer tools may work better
questions.explanation: Specific errors are necessary but not sufficient. Measure, then pick the fix that works for your model.

questions.question: The model put 'unit_from' (an argument of convert) on a call to lookup. What's a structural way to reduce this?
options: Offer only the tools relevant to the current step, so fewer schemas compete
questions.explanation: Argument bleed happens when many schemas are visible at once. Scoping tools per step or state (Lesson 9) reduces it.
